result.reason: The operative language gives Corio a 30-day written-notice convenience termination right, requires a pro-rata refund of prepaid recurring fees attributable to the post-termination period, eliminates termination charges and fee acceleration, and bars Commerce One from terminating for convenience during a committed term. This substantially reaches the preferred position. However, allowing termination “in whole or in part” creates an unnecessary partial-termination right not required by the playbook and may introduce scope and refund-allocation ambiguity. The refund language is also somewhat narrower than a refund of all prepaid fees because it is limited to recurring fees. Otherwise, the existing term and cause-termination provisions remain intact and the drafting is professional.
